title: Varicose veins and spider veins
intro: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins that are visible under the skin, mostly in the legs. Spider veins are tiny red or blue vessels at the surface. They are common, and often harmless, but can cause aching, heaviness and swelling. Many treatment options exist if they cause problems.

sections.heading: Causes and risk factors
paragraphs: Leg veins have valves that keep blood moving upward toward the heart. When valves weaken, blood pools and the vein widens. Risk factors include family history, age, being female, pregnancy, overweight, long periods of standing or sitting, and previous vein clots. Spider veins are mostly a cosmetic issue.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: Symptoms include visible bulging veins, an aching or heavy feeling, swelling of the ankles by the end of the day, itching, cramps at night and sometimes skin changes near the ankle. Symptoms are usually worse in the heat and after standing. Pain and redness along a vein may signal inflammation or a clot.

sections.heading: Complications
paragraphs: Possible complications include skin darkening and hardening, eczema, bleeding after a knock and open sores called venous ulcers. Superficial thrombophlebitis is a clot in a surface vein that causes a tender red cord. Sudden swelling, pain and warmth in the whole leg may indicate a deep vein clot and needs urgent assessment.

sections.heading: Self-care
paragraphs: Walk regularly, avoid long periods of standing or sitting, raise your legs when resting, maintain a healthy weight and consider compression stockings, which relieve symptoms for many people though they do not remove veins. Moisturise skin and protect it from injury. Simple measures help, but varicose veins do not go away without procedures.

sections.heading: Medical treatment
paragraphs: Treatments include sclerotherapy, in which a foam or liquid is injected to close veins, endovenous ablation using heat from a laser or radiofrequency, glue closure and surgery to tie off or remove veins. Most are done as outpatient procedures, with a return to daily activities within days. Treatment is advised for complications and persistent symptoms. Cosmetic treatment of spider veins is often paid privately. Veins can recur.

examples.title: Easing symptoms
examples.text: Imagine your legs feel heavy at the end of a working day. You could wear compression stockings, take breaks to walk and raise your legs in the evening.

examples.title: Choosing a procedure
examples.text: Suppose you are offered several treatments. You might ask how effective each is, recovery time, risks and the chance that veins return.
